highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially launched Claude Opus 5, now the default Opus model with a 1M token context window and a fast mode priced at $10/$50 per million tokens. This is a major upgrade for developers working on complex, long-context tasks inside Claude Code. If you use Claude Code, you'll automatically get Opus 5 when selecting the Opus tier.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219 Released — Opus 5 Default + Strict Network Sandbox
highlights.summary: This release adds Claude Opus 5 as the default Opus model in Claude Code and introduces a new `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` setting that blocks any non-allowlisted hosts for sandboxed commands without prompting. The new `DirectoryAdded` hook also gives developers more control over automation workflows when directories are added. Update Claude Code to take advantage of these features immediately.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.218 Released — /code-review Runs as Background Subagent
highlights.summary: The `/code-review` slash command now runs as a background subagent, meaning it no longer floods your main conversation context with review output. This keeps your conversation history clean and ensures stacked slash commands remain properly targeted for review. Developers doing frequent code reviews in long sessions will notice a significant workflow improvement.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.216 Released — Quadratic Slowdown Fix for Long Sessions
highlights.summary: This release patches a serious performance bug where message normalization cost grew quadratically with the number of turns, causing multi-second stalls and slow session resumes in long conversations. It also adds a `sandbox.filesystem.disabled` setting so you can skip filesystem isolation while still controlling network egress. If you've noticed Claude Code getting sluggish over long sessions, updating to this version should help significantly.

highlights.title: Claude Code Basics | Master 95% in 10 Minutes
highlights.summary: This short YouTube tutorial aims to cover the core 95% of Claude Code functionality in just 10 minutes, making it an efficient starting point for developers who want to get productive quickly. It's an ideal watch if you've just installed Claude Code and want a focused, no-fluff overview. Bookmark it to share with teammates who are new to AI-assisted coding.

highlights.title: The New Way Top Anthropic Engineers Prompt Claude Code
highlights.summary: This video reveals prompting strategies used by Anthropic's own engineers to get the best results from Claude Code, offering insider techniques you won't find in the official docs. Learning how the people who built the tool actually use it can help you adopt better habits early and avoid common pitfalls. Intermediate users who already know the basics will get the most value from this one.

highlights.title: Show HN: claude-account — Switch Claude Code Accounts Without Logging In Again
highlights.summary: A developer built a small CLI tool that lets you save and switch between multiple Claude Code accounts instantly, without going through the full login flow each time. This is especially handy if you maintain separate accounts for work and personal projects. Install it with a few commands and use `claude account add` to register each account.

highlights.title: How Does Claude Code Actually Work? Let's Make Our Own
highlights.summary: This deep-dive YouTube video explores the internals of Claude Code by walking through building a similar tool from scratch, giving you a much stronger mental model of how Claude Code operates under the hood. Understanding these mechanics can help you configure Claude Code more effectively and debug unexpected behaviors. Advanced developers or curious learners who want to go beyond surface-level usage will find this especially rewarding.

tips_of_the_day: If your Claude Code sessions feel slow after many turns, update to v2.1.216 or later — a quadratic performance bug in long conversations has been fixed, and you'll notice much snappier responses and faster session resumes.

Use the `/code-review` slash command freely without worrying about polluting your conversation history — since v2.1.218 it runs as a background subagent, so your main context stays clean and focused on your actual coding work.

If you work with multiple Claude accounts (personal vs. work), set them up once using a tool like claude-account so you can switch instantly from the terminal — no more logging out and back in every time you context-switch between projects.
